title: Trust nothing. Verify everything.
Us too.
lead: At DFNS, zero trust security is an architectural constraint with a precise meaning. No statement is believed because of who said it, every request, approval, and signature must carry its own cryptographic proof.

cards.title: Every request is signed
cards.body: No session cookies. A passkey signs each action at origin, intercepting traffic earns an attacker nothing.

cards.title: Every approval is proof
cards.body: Quorum decisions are cryptographic artifacts, committed and verifiable, not rows in a database an admin could edit.

cards.title: No key is ever exposed
cards.body: Key material is born sharded and stays sharded; there is no moment, on any machine, where the complete key exists to steal.

cards.title: Signers believe no one
cards.body: The signing layer independently re-verifies the entire chain of intent. A fully compromised application layer still cannot sign.

cards.title: DFNS is inside the threat model
cards.body: The system is engineered so that we cannot move your assets; our own staff face the same gauntlet as everyone else.

strip.author: Thibault de Lachèze-Murel
strip.text: “We built DFNS assuming that one day, someone we trust, an employee, a vendor, even ourselves, would become the attacker. Everything follows from that assumption.”
